expectation.management: Permethrin 5% cream applied neck-to-toe, repeated in one week; treatment of the roommate and laundering of shared bedding; itch can persist for weeks after cure.

P.name: Arun
P.publicProfile: Male, 19, first-year student living in the university hostel. Presents with an intensely itchy rash between his fingers and wrists that is much worse at night and has been troubling him for about three weeks.
P.secret: Embarrassed to say his roommate has the same itch; he shares bedding. He has been scratching so much that his skin is raw in places.

clues.label: Intensely itchy rash
clues.shortText: Intensely itchy rash for ~3 weeks, far worse at night.
clues.longText: Arun has had an intensely itchy rash for about three weeks. It keeps him awake at night — the itching is far worse then.

clues.label: Rash between fingers
clues.shortText: Rash concentrated between the fingers and on the wrists.
clues.longText: The rash is worst between his fingers and on the inner wrists, with a few spots around the waist.

clues.label: Health room logged itch
clues.shortText: Hostel health room logged the itch complaint 2 weeks ago.
clues.longText: The hostel health room note records that Arun came in for itching two weeks ago and was given a calamine lotion that did not help.

clues.label: Itch worse at night
clues.shortText: Itching peaks after lights out — keeps him from sleeping.
clues.longText: Arun's itching peaks at night once he is in bed; he has scratched until his skin is raw in places.

clues.label: Fine burrows on exam
clues.shortText: Fine wavy grey lines (burrows) in the finger web spaces.
clues.longText: On examination there are fine wavy grey burrows in the finger web spaces, with excoriations from scratching.

clues.label: Roommate also itches
clues.shortText: Roommate Rohit has been itching for 2 weeks too.
clues.longText: Arun's roommate Rohit has been itching for about two weeks as well — which is why Arun finally came to the clinic.

clues.label: No eczema history
clues.shortText: File shows no prior eczema or allergy history.
clues.longText: The health-room file contains no history of eczema, asthma or allergy in Arun — his skin was previously clear.

clues.label: Excoriations from scratching
clues.shortText: Raw, excoriated skin from repeated scratching.
clues.longText: Arun shows raw, excoriated patches where he has scratched, mostly over the wrists and finger webs.

clues.label: Shared bedding/clothes
clues.shortText: They share a quilt and trade clothes — the transmission route.
clues.longText: Rohit admits they share a bed-quilt and swap clothes, and the bedding has not been washed in weeks — the likely route the mite spread.

clues.label: Skin photo: burrows
clues.shortText: Clinical photo confirms burrows between the fingers.
clues.longText: The clinical photograph of the finger web spaces shows the fine wavy burrows of scabies with surrounding excoriation.

clues.label: KOH scraping: mites
clues.shortText: Skin scraping shows Sarcoptes scabiei mites and eggs.
clues.longText: The KOH skin scraping from a finger web burrow shows Sarcoptes scabiei mite fragments and eggs — microscopically confirmed scabies.

clues.label: DIAGNOSIS
clues.longText: Scabies. Arun is started on permethrin cream and both he and Rohit are treated together; their bedding is washed. His relief is immediate once the night itching finally stops.
